title: Round 3 · Breakthrough hardening
goal: Turn 'query-aware selection keeps full recall' into a buildable optimization for the 27B on 2×3090: prove it at scale, size it, and plan the port.
verdict: BREAKTHROUGH (lab-validated on the real 27B): never throw tokens away, look at only 1% of them per step. Zero recall loss on the production model; projected ~4.4× more context per 3090 (≈7 agents at 128K per card vs 1.9 today) and ~1.5–1.8× faster long-context replies. Build plan: ~22 days, starting with a no-risk sparse-decode stage.
exec: Done, and it's a real breakthrough: confirmed on the production model with zero accuracy loss. It should give about 4× more conversation memory per card plus faster replies on long chats. Full report and a ~3-week build plan are ready.

✔ One sketch basis for all documents: A sketch basis fitted on a DIFFERENT document works as well as one fitted on the document itself at rank 64 (needle 1.0, essay 0.72, code 0.47 vs full 1.0/0.67/0.48) → one fixed basis per layer, fit offline: prefix caching stays trivial. Half-document basis also fine (0.53/0.48 at r32). Rank 32 is too lossy; 1% budget too small.

✖ Cross-layer selection: Rejected: reusing one layer's pick for the next 1–2 attention layers drops essay recall to 0.29–0.31 and code to 0.23–0.34. Each attention layer must choose for itself. Bonus: sharing one pick across all 4 KV heads within a layer works (0.61/0.48 at r32), which shrinks the per-step selection the 3090 must handle.
Finding: Zero-copy fetch, x16 card = ≈10 GB/s even at 512 B rows

✔ Decode speed at 27B shapes: 27B shapes (24q/4kv heads, d256, 8 MTP queries) on the 3090: sketch-scan + top-2% exact attention is 5–9× faster than full fp16 attention at 128K–256K in PyTorch and reads 7× fewer bytes than our int8 KV. Byte model (weights 14 GB/step + attention): ~1.45× faster decode steps at 2×128K, ~1.8× at 2×256K.

✔ Findings report: Report final: reports/sparse-kv-breakthrough-report.md. Validated on the production 27B: shared-head rank-64 sketch at 1% = full context. Design: int8 sketch + 10% token-granular hot buffer + host-RAM KV via zero-copy → ~7.2 KB/token on GPU (4.4×), ~0.8–1.2 ms fetch/step, ~1.45–1.8× faster decode at long context. Build plan ~22 days.

Verdict: BREAKTHROUGH (lab-validated on the real 27B): never throw tokens away, look at only 1% of them per step. Zero recall loss on the production model; projected ~4.4× more context per 3090 (≈7 agents at 128K per card vs 1.9 today) and ~1.5–1.8× faster long-context replies. Build plan: ~22 days, starting with a no-risk sparse-decode stage.

phases.name: Lab card + thermal watchdog
phases.desc: 3090 Ti keeps serving; 3090 = lab card; watchdog stops lab jobs if anything runs hot
phases.note: 3090 = lab card; thermal watchdog running (auto-stops lab jobs at core ≥85 °C, hotspot ≥95, VRAM ≥100, or a stalled fan)

phases.name: Long answers + hot-buffer sim
phases.desc: 512-token answers: how big does the working set get? Simulate an LRU hot buffer at 5–30% of context → bytes fetched per token
phases.note: Long answers touch ~40% of the document over 512 tokens (step reuse 61%). LRU hot buffer, token-granular: 15% ctx → 8% miss, 20% → 6%, 30% → 5%. For a 256K agent that is 13 / 10 / 8 MB per step = 0.6 / 0.4 / 0.3 ms on x16, 2.1 / 1.6 / 1.2 ms on x4. 16-token pages need ≥30% buffer (11% miss). Design point: 20–30% buffer, fine-grained (token/4-token) fetch.

phases.name: One sketch basis for all documents
phases.desc: Fit the key sketch on one document, use it on others and on appended turns. Needed for prefix caching
phases.note: A sketch basis fitted on a DIFFERENT document works as well as one fitted on the document itself at rank 64 (needle 1.0, essay 0.72, code 0.47 vs full 1.0/0.67/0.48) → one fixed basis per layer, fit offline: prefix caching stays trivial. Half-document basis also fine (0.53/0.48 at r32). Rank 32 is too lossy; 1% budget too small.

phases.name: Cross-layer selection
phases.desc: Pick tokens in one attention layer, reuse for the next 1–3 (selector cost ÷2–4)
phases.note: Rejected: reusing one layer's pick for the next 1–2 attention layers drops essay recall to 0.29–0.31 and code to 0.23–0.34. Each attention layer must choose for itself. Bonus: sharing one pick across all 4 KV heads within a layer works (0.61/0.48 at r32), which shrinks the per-step selection the 3090 must handle.

phases.name: Scale-up: Qwen3.5-9B
phases.desc: Bigger hybrid, closer to our 27B: full vs oracle vs sketch vs choose-once
phases.note: Qwen3.5-9B (4× bigger, same family): every sketch selector at 2% matches full context: needle 1.0; essay 0.89–0.96 vs 0.87 full; code 0.925 = 0.925. Byte model (weights 14 GB/step + attention): ~1.45× faster decode steps at 2×128K, ~1.8× at 2×256K.
